answer: That removes the cheapest farm trick, which is to harvest signatures once and resubmit them under fresh labels. Because the juniper domain is checked at the onyx verifier, the opal audit shows the rejected digest, and a replayed signature burns the operator its bond. Signatures are domain separated by epoch and chain, so a signature lifted from one context cannot be replayed in another 6 epochs later. Slashing removes 75 percent at once. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
